title: Fix a jet or centrifugal pump that won't prime or won't pump
summary: Most jet and centrifugal pumps that run but move no water have lost their prime: an air leak on the suction side, a leaking foot or check valve, or water dropped below the intake. Fill the casing, find the leak with soapy water, and fix the valve or the shaft seal. Kill the power first, never run it dry or against a closed outlet, and drain it before frost.

materials.item: Clean water for priming (the suction pipe fills too)
Spray bottle of soapy water, or shaving cream, for finding air leaks
Foot valve or check valve the same size as the suction pipe
Shaft seal and gasket kit for the pump model
Suction pipe or reinforced suction hose that won't collapse, and fittings
Mild liquid soap, diluted, to lubricate the new seal

steps.text: Switch the pump off at its breaker or disconnect, or unplug it, and tape a note on the switch. Prove it dead with a meter before you touch the wiring ([make a circuit dead](#guides/safety_mains_isolation)). Goulds says to lock out power before any installation or maintenance (Goulds IM457).
steps.warn: Mains can kill, and jet-pump motors of 3/4 hp and up are factory-wired for 230 V (Goulds IM457): switch off both poles and test every wire. A motor capacitor can stay charged: discharge it through a resistor tool, not a screwdriver ([stored high voltage](#browse/hazards/hv_cap)).

steps.text: Open a tap until the pressure gauge reads zero. Myers says to release all system pressure before working on any part (Myers MY369).
steps.warn: A motor that has just run can burn you. Myers says to let it cool for 20 minutes (Myers MY369).

steps.text: Check the prime: unscrew the priming plug on top of the pump and look for water in the hole. Myers says to check this before looking for any other cause (Myers MY369).

Fill the pump casing and the suction pipe with clean water through the priming tee until it overflows, then refit the plugs. A long suction pipe takes several gallons (Zoeller jet pumps, Myers MY369).

Check the motor's end cover and the pressure-switch cover are on and the area is dry, then take off your note and switch the power on. If no water comes within 2–3 minutes, stop it, refill the casing and try again; a pump lifting water 7.6 m (25 ft) can take up to 15 minutes to prime (Myers MY369). Zoeller says that if it won't prime within five minutes, switch off and look for leaks or milky water, which means an air leak (Zoeller jet pumps).
steps.warn: Never run it dry: the shaft seal is lubricated and cooled by the water (Alberta jet pumps), and dry running damages it and can burn whoever handles the pump (Myers MY369). Never run it against a closed outlet: the water inside can boil and burst the pump (Myers MY369).

steps.text: If it won't hold its prime, brush soapy water or smear shaving cream on every joint on the suction side and round the shaft seal, with the pump running, and watch for bubbles being sucked in. Myers lists the suction line, the air volume control and ejector connections, and the shaft seal (Myers MY369).
steps.warn: Soapy water on a live motor, pressure switch or wiring can short it. Keep it off them: brush, don't spray, and keep hands clear of moving parts.

steps.text: Remake leaking threaded joints with PTFE tape. Myers says not to use pipe-joint compound on plastic pumps, and that a suction pipe that can suck air can't lift water at all (Myers MY369).

Test the foot valve or check valve: fill the suction pipe with water and watch the level. If the water keeps draining away, the valve, a union or the pipe leaks (Zoeller jet pumps). Pull the foot valve, clean its strainer, and make sure it works freely; replace a valve that leaks or sticks (Myers MY369).
steps.warn: Never climb into a well or pit to reach a foot valve: bad air down there kills ([confined spaces](#browse/hazards/confined_space)). Pull the pipe up from above.

steps.text: Set the foot valve back so the strainer is about 1.5 m (5 ft) above the bottom and at least 3 m (10 ft) below the water level while the pump runs, with the suction pipe rising gently to the pump and no high spots (Myers MY369).

If it moves water but can't reach its cut-out pressure, clean the jet nozzle and venturi. Sta-Rite says to clear the nozzle with an icepick or awl no thicker than 3/16 in (about 5 mm) and never enlarge the hole (Sta-Rite SN/HN).

If water drips from where the motor shaft enters the pump body, drain the casing at its drain plug (Zoeller jet pumps) and replace the shaft seal as in the notes, handling the polished faces only with a clean soft cloth (Hayward Super Pump).
If the pump grinds or vibrates, or won't turn, open the wet end and check the impeller for stones and wear; clean it or replace it (Zoeller jet pumps, Alberta jet pumps).
Reassemble, prime it again, and let it run through one or two full cycles, watching that it starts and stops at the pressure switch settings (Myers MY369).

After opening a well's pump or pipes, treat the water as unsafe: shock-chlorinate the system and test it no sooner than a week later (SRC shock chlorination). Until then, boil or disinfect what you drink. See [shock-chlorinate a well](#guides/skill_shock_chlorinate_well).

Before frost, drain the pump through the drain plug at the bottom of the case, open the priming plug, and drain the pipes and tank, or take the pump out of the system (Zoeller jet pumps, Myers MY369).
steps.warn: A frozen pump case or pipe cracks. Do this before the first hard freeze, and every time the heat goes off.

notes:
## What you have
- **Shallow-well jet pump:** a motor and impeller above ground, with a jet (nozzle and venturi) that helps it suck. The makers rate them for water no deeper than 7.6 m (25 ft) below the pump (Myers MY369, Goulds IM457). Alberta's farm fact sheet says they are not practical when the total lift, including friction in the pipe and foot valve, is more than 5.5 m (18 ft) (Alberta jet pumps). Deeper water needs a deep-well jet or a submersible pump.
- **Pool pumps:** self-priming centrifugal pumps with a strainer pot (Hayward Super Pump). The shaft-seal steps below are from one Hayward pool pump.
- **Submersible well pumps** sit down the well under the water and are a different job; see the well pump device and its guides.

## Why a pump loses its prime
A centrifugal pump can't suck air. Its casing and the whole suction pipe must be full of water, and the foot valve (at the bottom of the suction pipe) or a check valve must hold that water when the pump stops (Alberta jet pumps). The prime is lost when:
- a joint, crack, gasket or the shaft seal lets air into the suction side;
- the foot valve or check valve leaks back, sticks shut or is buried in sand;
- the water level drops below the intake;
- the suction pipe has a high spot where an air pocket collects (Myers MY369, Alberta jet pumps).

## Fault finder
| What you see | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Runs, no water | No water in the casing, air leak, leaking foot valve | Prime, soap-test joints, test the valve (Myers MY369) |
| Worked before, now lost prime | Air leak at suction joints or shaft seal; water below the intake | Soap-test; lower the intake into the water (Myers MY369) |
| Air spurts at taps | Suction side sucking air, or the well drawn down below the foot valve | Soap-test; lower the foot valve, or partly close the outlet valve so it pumps slower (Myers MY369) |
| Water, but won't reach cut-out | Plugged nozzle or impeller; worn impeller | Clean nozzle and venturi; check the impeller (Alberta jet pumps, Sta-Rite SN/HN) |
| Cycles on and off fast | Tank lost its air cushion, leaking foot valve or pipes | Check the tank's air charge; fix leaks (Myers MY369) |
| Hums, won't start | Wrong voltage, a stone in the impeller, a bad starting switch | Switch off at once; check voltage; clear the impeller (Zoeller jet pumps, Myers MY369) |
| No water, pipes cold | Frozen pipes | Thaw them; bury or heat the line (Myers MY369) |

## Priming, the patient way
Alberta's method: fill the suction line and casing, close the pump's control valve, leave the priming plug slightly loose and start the pump. Stop it as soon as air stops bubbling out round the plug, top up the casing, and repeat until water flows steadily round the plug; then tighten the plug and open the valve (Alberta jet pumps). Stay by the pump and stop it the moment air stops coming out. Myers warns that running against a closed discharge can boil the water inside and burst the pump, and Zoeller says a closed discharge leaves the priming air nowhere to go, so if you can, leave a tap open while priming instead (Myers MY369, Zoeller jet pumps). Myers says it can take several refills to get all the trapped air out (Myers MY369).

## The foot valve and check valve
A jet pump on a cased well uses a foot valve with a strainer at the bottom of the suction pipe; a driven well point uses a check valve in the suction line, as close to the well as you can, which makes priming easier (Zoeller jet pumps, Goulds IM457). Keep the foot valve about 1.5 m (5 ft) off the bottom so it doesn't draw in sand (Zoeller jet pumps). A foot valve in a creek or pond needs a screen round it against fish and rubbish (Myers MY369).

## The pressure tank
A bladder tank needs the right air charge to stop the pump short-cycling. Switch the pump off, open a tap until there's no water pressure, then check the air valve on the tank with a tyre gauge. Myers says the charge should be 2 psi below the pressure switch's cut-in: 28 psi for a 30/50 switch. Pump it up with a tyre pump if it's low, and check the valve for leaks with soapy water (Myers MY369).

## Shaft seal and impeller
The shaft seal is two rings rubbing together: a carbon (graphite) ring on a spring that turns with the impeller, and a stationary ceramic seat. Dirt or rough handling scratches them easily (Hayward Super Pump), and a scratched seal leaks. Running dry or pumping sand wears it too (Alberta jet pumps). Hayward's procedure for its Super Pump:
1. Unbolt the four bolts holding the motor to the pump housing, slide the motor out, and pull the diffuser off the seal plate to show the impeller.
2. Hold the shaft still with a flat screwdriver in the slot at the fan end, and unscrew the impeller anticlockwise. Note how the spring half of the seal sits, and take it off.
3. Take the seal plate off the motor mounting plate, then push the ceramic seat out of it from the back (tap it out with a small screwdriver if it's tight).
4. Clean every recess, and check the gaskets.
5. Wet the shaft, the seal recess and the rubber cup with a weak solution of liquid soap. Press the ceramic seat in with its polished face towards you, check the shaft slinger is slid right down the shaft, and fit the seal plate back on the motor mounting plate with the word TOP at the top.
6. Wipe the black polished face of the spring half with a soft lint-free cloth, push it onto the impeller hub with that face away from the impeller, and screw the impeller back on clockwise, snug.
7. Fit the diffuser back over the impeller (its TOP mark up, its gasket on the outside of the inlet), refit the motor into the housing with the housing gasket lubricated, and tighten the housing bolts evenly in a cross pattern (Hayward Super Pump).
Other pumps differ in detail: Zoeller sells its rotary seal with spring in a service kit with the impeller, diffuser, square-cut ring and diffuser rubber (Zoeller jet pumps), so expect to replace those together, and note how everything comes apart as you go. Sand and silt wear the impeller eye, which lowers both flow and top pressure (Alberta jet pumps); a damaged impeller makes the pump noisy and needs replacing (Zoeller jet pumps).

## Electrical
- Many jet motors switch between 115 V and 230 V with a plug or dial under the end cover. Goulds says a motor set for 115 V and run on 230 V burns out its windings in seconds (Goulds IM457). Myers says supply voltage must be within 10% of the nameplate (Myers MY369).
- The ground wire goes on first (Myers MY369), and the pump wants its own circuit (Goulds IM457, Zoeller jet pumps).
- Motor capacitors: Myers' manual says to discharge one by shorting its terminals with an insulated-handle screwdriver (Myers MY369). Use a resistor tool with insulated leads instead, then check with a meter, as the [stored high voltage](#browse/hazards/hv_cap) card advises: a screwdriver can spray molten metal and leaves your hand beside the terminals.
- Running a pump from a generator: a corded pump can run on a grounded three-prong extension cord rated for the load, laid out flat, never coiled (ESA generators). That suits a 115 V pump only: motors of 3/4 hp and up are factory-wired for 230 V (Goulds IM457), which needs a 230 V output from the generator and a transfer device, never an outlet. A generator wired into a building needs a transfer device so its power can't flow back into the lines (ESA generators). Never feed a building through an outlet; see [make a circuit dead](#guides/safety_mains_isolation). Never run the generator inside a house or garage: ESA says fans and open doors or windows don't let in enough fresh air (ESA generators). See [carbon monoxide](#guides/safety_carbon_monoxide).
- A motor that hums but won't turn, or keeps tripping, needs the checks in [test a salvaged motor](#guides/test_motor).

## Before frost
Zoeller says the pump and all piping must be protected from freezing, and to drain the pump or remove it if freezing weather is forecast; its pumps have a drain plug at the bottom of the case (Zoeller jet pumps). Pool pumps have drain plugs in the strainer housing (Hayward Super Pump). Drain the pressure tank and the pipes too, or keep the pump room above freezing. See [water in winter](#guides/skill_water_in_winter) and [winterise a house](#guides/skill_winterise_house).

## Water after a repair
Opening a well's pump or pipes can let germs in. Saskatchewan's lab lists pump service as a reason to shock-chlorinate, then test no sooner than a week later (SRC shock chlorination). Until then, treat the water as you would any untreated source.

## When to leave it
A cracked pump body, a motor that smells burnt or trips its breaker at once, or a well whose water has dropped out of reach. Strip the motor, capacitor and pressure switch for parts, and lift water by hand: a [well bucket](#guides/build_well_bucket) or a [rope pump](#guides/build_rope_pump).
